comparator.name: Biomedical Sciences (Biomedische Wetenschappen)
comparator.academicYear: Adopted Biomedical Sciences OER 2026–27, articles 11–12 and current 2026–27 study guide; checked 2026-09-26
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–27 OER lists nine compulsory 6-EC year-one components plus one 6-EC restricted choice, nine compulsory 6-EC year-two components plus a separate 6-EC restricted choice, and year three with 30 EC genuinely open minor space, one 6-EC restricted choice and one of two mutually exclusive 24-EC thesis formats. The first-listed option in the formally adopted OER is instantiated at each choice point: Biomedical Sciences and Society, Pathophysiology of Heart and Circulation, Epidemiology, and the Experimental thesis. The study-guide display order differs from OER in the year-one and year-three choice lists; the OER order supplies the neutral choices. Zero-credit lab safety and language assessment are excluded. Optional minors and thesis formats are not formal named graduation routes. The general prospective page refers to the forthcoming 2027–28 intake, so the 2026–27 OER governs this comparator.
components: First-listed of three restricted 6-EC year-one choices (Biomedische Wetenschappen en de Maatschappij, Science Communication, Biochemisch onderzoek); selected for this valid pathway.
First-listed of four restricted 6-EC year-two choices (Pathophysiology of heart and circulation, Big data, International Public Health, Science Communication).
Genuinely open academic 30-EC third-year minor/profiling space; no optional minor is imposed.
First-listed of four restricted 6-EC year-three choices in the adopted OER (Epidemiology, Human Neurophysiology, Management of Innovations, Infectious Diseases).
Required 24-EC thesis choice: Experimental selected rather than the mutually exclusive Data Analysis thesis.

questions: How do cellular and immune mechanisms produce disease and guide treatment?
How can public-health evidence improve prevention and care across populations?
How can biomedical data reveal and predict disease processes?

alternatives.label: Human biology, disease and biomedical research
alternatives.concept: Combines molecular and cellular biology, anatomy and physiology, immunity, pharmacology, disease mechanisms and neuroscience with laboratory, statistical and ethical study. It reflects the compulsory VU core while UCR lacks dedicated oncology, omics and a 24-EC experimental thesis placement.
alternatives.labelReason: Human body systems, disease mechanisms, biomedical laboratory work and research methods dominate the completed course set.
progression: Every course meets Fall 2026–Spring 2029 availability, formal prerequisite order and the six-semester workload. Life and brain gateway courses precede advanced disease or neuroscience work; introductory programming and mathematics precede computational methods where required. Advisory progression was reviewed.

alternatives.label: Public health, disease prevention and interventions
alternatives.concept: Studies illness across body systems and populations, combining epidemiology, immunology, human physiology, health psychology, social conditions, health financing and research methods. The organising question shifts from laboratory mechanisms toward prevention and evaluation of interventions.
alternatives.labelReason: Epidemiology, health psychology, sociology, public economics and communication make population-level prevention a substantial academic centre.
alternatives.distinctness: Eight courses differ from the biomedical core route, adding sociology, health psychology, qualitative research, public economics and persuasion while reducing specialist neuroscience, anatomy and mathematical/computational methods.
progression: Every course meets Fall 2026–Spring 2029 availability, formal prerequisite order and the six-semester workload. Life and brain gateway courses precede advanced disease or neuroscience work; introductory programming and mathematics precede computational methods where required. Advisory progression was reviewed.

alternatives.label: Biomedical data and quantitative disease models
alternatives.concept: Connects cellular and physiological disease study with programming, mathematical modelling, image analysis, machine learning and neural networks. These are general UCR computational methods applied to biomedical questions, not a substitute for VU omics laboratory training or the data-analysis thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The course set contains a sustained computing, mathematical and data sequence alongside body systems and disease biology.
alternatives.distinctness: Five courses differ from the closest biomedical route and twelve from public health: image processing, deep learning, linear algebra, numerical methods and signal systems displace several pharmacology, neurobehavioral and clinical research elements, materially changing the analytical tools.
progression: Every course meets Fall 2026–Spring 2029 availability, formal prerequisite order and the six-semester workload. Life and brain gateway courses precede advanced disease or neuroscience work; introductory programming and mathematics precede computational methods where required. Advisory progression was reviewed.

candidates.label: Global public health and biomedical intervention
Biomedical data analysis and predictive models

selection.assessment: The broad biomedical route, population-health interventions, and quantitative biomedical analysis arise sequentially from distinct target-specific evidence. Each produces a coherent 24-course curriculum, passes workbook feasibility and changes at least five courses against every other route. The data direction explicitly preserves the gap in VU omics and the formal thesis.

Both introduce biomedical foundations from cells to body systems.

Both study molecular biochemistry and metabolism.
Both address genetic mechanisms in human disease; UCR combines pathology and genetics.

notes.text: VU requires a prescribed molecular, anatomical and clinical sequence, three separately restricted 6-EC choices, and a 24-EC experimental or data-analysis research thesis alongside an open 30-EC minor. UCR can combine biomedical, public-health and data study but does not duplicate specialised oncology, omics, microbiology laboratory or the VU thesis placement.
